Detect the encoding of bytes

Source: R/convert.R
utf_detect.Rd

Lists the encodings each element could be in. A byte-order mark decides alone; otherwise the candidates are every encoding the bytes are valid in, by the validators of simdutf, in the order UTF-8, UTF-16LE, UTF-16BE, UTF-32LE, UTF-32BE. Latin-1 is never listed, since every byte string is valid Latin-1, and pure ASCII text is valid UTF-16 too when its length is even, which is why UTF-8 comes first.

Usage

utf_detect(x)

Arguments

x

A raw vector (one element) or a list of raw vectors.

Value

For a raw vector, a character vector of candidate encodings, best first, and character(0) when none fits. For a list, a list of such vectors (NULL for a NULL element), keeping its names.

See also

utf_decode(), whose from = "auto" takes the first candidate.

Examples

utf_detect(charToRaw("hello"))
#> [1] "UTF-8"
utf_detect(as.raw(c(0xff, 0xfe, 0x68, 0x00)))   # a UTF-16LE BOM
#> [1] "UTF-16LE"
utf_detect(as.raw(c(0xff, 0xff, 0xff)))
#> character(0)
